doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lineage of drumming styles since the 1950s
summary: Brown traces Haynes to DeJohnette to Erskine and Tony Williams to fusion; Haynes says little has been different since Trane.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Just looking back on the development of jazz drumming, or maybe swing-based jazz drumming, coming out, since you have the whole perspective, since you were there when it started, and we’re here today. You have people who come along who basically shape the direction. I would say that Tony Williams was very important. Who else would you say whose unique style may have been . . .?
Um-hmm. Just drums. Or if you want to talk about jazz in general.
What do you mean? Some of the older drummers? Or the younger since him?
I would say since the ’50s, since the ’60s. Unless you – I’m looking back at the development and looking at who’s styles basically shaped the direction.
I don’t think no one person’s style shaped the direction. I don’t think.

Not determined the direction, but helped to shape the direction. For example, looking in the ’40s, Bu, Max, Klook, and others of course. Then in the ’50s with Philly Joe. Yourself ’40s and ’50s, but probably more so in the ’50s, your style. Then your style spawns people like Elvin and Jack. Jack is very important. To me, I can listen to guys like Peter Erskine and know exactly where he came from. He comes from Jack and Jack comes from you. If you study it stylistically, you could see this lineage.
That’s something where you could see it. Maybe I don’t listen to them enough to be able to tell that. But it’s interesting

People coming out of Tony. You can trace who comes out of Tony, because the whole – a lot of the fusion school comes out of that. But I’m just trying to see if you have a particular perspective on that.
No. No I don’t. I do not.
How about on the music in general? On jazz in general.
Since Trane. Let’s say, since Trane.
It ain’t nothing to me. It’s a little bit different since Trane. So I’m going to leave it alone.
